title: Undergraduate Course Allocation through Competitive Markets
abstract: arXiv:2412.05691v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Prevailing methods of course allocation at undergraduate institutions involve reserving seats to give priority to designated groups of students. We present a competitive equilibrium-based mechanism that assigns course seats using student preferences and course priorities. This mechanism satisfies approximate notions of stability, efficiency, envy-freeness, and strategy-proofness. We evaluate its performance relative to a mechanism widely used in practice using preferences estimated from university data. Our empirical findings demonstrate an improvement in student satisfaction and allocation fairness. The number of students who envy another student of weakly lower priority declines by 8 percentage points, or roughly 500 students.

translated_title: 基于竞争市场的本科生课程分配
translated_abstract: 当前本科院校普遍采用的课程分配方法通常通过预留名额来给予特定学生群体优先权。我们提出了一种基于竞争均衡的机制，利用学生偏好和课程优先级来分配课程名额。该机制满足稳定性的近似概念、效率、无嫉妒性和防策略性。我们利用从大学数据中估计出的学生偏好，将该机制与实践广泛使用的机制进行了性能对比评估。实证结果表明，该机制提升了学生满意度和分配公平性：嫉妒优先级较弱的其他学生的学生数量下降了8个百分点，即约500名学生。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于竞争均衡的本科课程分配机制，在满足近似的稳定性、效率、无嫉妒性和防策略性的同时，实证表明学生满意度与分配公平性显著提升，嫉妒弱低优先级同学的学生数量减少约8个百分点（约500人）。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a competitive equilibrium-based mechanism for undergraduate course allocation that approximately satisfies stability, efficiency, envy-freeness, and strategy-proofness, with empirical results showing improved student satisfaction and fairness, reducing the number of students envying weakly lower-priority peers by 8 percentage points (roughly 500 students).
